result.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Continual World Models Workshop
result.summary: Continual learning treats degradation on previously seen data as evidence of failure, a convention inherited from settings with a stationary prediction target, where a correct label remains correct indefinitely. World models do not satisfy this condition. Their prediction target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when acquired may later become false, and discarding it is required behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode knowledge that must never be revised. We argue that continual world models require retention stratified by invariance timescale, separating invariants such as physics and object permanence, which must never be revised, from instance-level facts that should be revised as soon as the environment changes. Standard forgetting metrics cannot distinguish a world model that has correctly revised outdated knowledge from one that has suffered catastrophic forgetting, and consequently rank a frozen model highest, while existing physical-reasoning benchmarks evaluate only frozen checkpoints. We propose differential retention, which reports invariant regression testing across the adaptation stream jointly with revision latency, without aggregation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文区分「不应被修改的物理/客体恒常性不变量」与「应随环境变化即时修订的实例级事实」，提出按不变性时间尺度分层的保留评测，即同时报告不变量回归测试与修订延迟且不做聚合。
AI.relevance_reason: 世界模型中的不变量知识是否需要、何时需要修订，可能可迁移到 LVR 的停止决策与状态更新问题：latent 推理状态中哪些内容应稳定保留、哪些应在证据变化时被覆盖，以及如何避免用单一聚合指标误判「正确修订」与「信息坍缩」，可供核查。另注意该工作面向世界模型与模型评测，与 VLM 推理主线距离较远。
